definition: Source trustworthiness is the degree to which a person sees an information source, such as an expert source, as credible and worthy of trust. In this context, greater perceived trustworthiness can increase how effective a message seems and support acceptance of the recommendation even when detailed evidence is limited.

reasons: The packet describes an experimental manipulation of “source trustworthiness” (trust-building appeals) and relates it to outcomes like perceived message effectiveness and pro-vaccine beliefs, but it does not explicitly define “source trustworthiness” as “the degree to which a person sees an information source… as credible and worthy of trust.”

The claim that “greater perceived trustworthiness can increase how effective a message seems” is broadly consistent with the reported significant effects on perceived message effectiveness, but the definition’s first sentence still contains an unsupported definitional characterization not provided in the packet.

The statement that acceptance can be supported “even when detailed evidence is limited” is only partially supported; the packet reports that establishing trust may reduce the need to describe available evidence, and that evidence can influence acceptance even among those with lower trust, but it does not directly support the specific phrasing about “detailed evidence” being limited.
